name: Ordinary Portland Cement (OPC 43 / OPC 53 Repair Mortar)
traditional_use: Modern 20th-century unscientific repair; pointing, plastering, and structural patching.

moisture_behavior.capillary_suction: Dense micro-porous structure blocks vapor transmission
moisture_behavior.drying_rate: Very slow; forces trapped water into adjacent porous stone units
moisture_behavior.summary: Acts as an impermeable moisture dam, trapping rising damp inside historic walls and forcing salt crystallization behind the cement crust.

mechanical_characteristics.stiffness: Excessively high stiffness (20-35 GPa), 5 to 10 times stiffer than historic lime mortar
mechanical_characteristics.ductility: Brittle, zero plastic yield under low stress
mechanical_characteristics.sacrificial_behavior: Anti-sacrificial: significantly stronger than historic sandstone, lakhori brick, and lime mortar
mechanical_characteristics.summary: Transfers all thermal and structural movement stresses directly into historic stone edges, causing fracture and spalling.

thermal_characteristics.thermal_shock_resilience: High rigidity induces shear delamination under diurnal heating
thermal_characteristics.compatibility_with_historic_stones: High differential thermal expansion relative to soft historic stones
thermal_characteristics.summary: Shears away from host stone during hot-cold cycles, creating open fissures that admit rainwater.

chemical_considerations.soluble_salts_risk: Introduces harmful soluble sodium and potassium sulfates (alkali-sulfate compounds)
chemical_considerations.reactivity_with_limestone: Chemical reaction between cement sulfates and limestone forms expansive ettringite and thaumasite
chemical_considerations.summary: Expansive mineral formation causes destructive cryptoflorescence and crumble of adjacent historic stone.

reversibility.extraction_method: Extremely difficult; requires rotary diamond cutter or heavy chisel, inevitably cutting and scarring original stone arrises
reversibility.retreatability: Irreversible; removal often causes more mechanical damage than leaving it undisturbed without specialist conservators

heritage_compatibility.iks_alignment: Zero alignment; completely alien to traditional Indian hydraulic masonry science
heritage_compatibility.asi_intach_compliance: Explicitly prohibited by ASI Conservation Manual (2020) and INTACH Charter (2004) on historic stone

limitations: Contextual evaluation: OPC is not universally evil in modern reinforced concrete construction, but when applied to historic breathing masonry, its physical mismatch causes severe degradation.
Removing existing sound cement patches must be evaluated on a case-by-case basis to prevent tearing away friable stone face.
